## The expert file through the OS file cache when needed; the launchers tell Iris Xe / UHD from Meteor Lake

- **A mixture-of-experts model's expert file is read through the OS file cache when it helps.** That is when the GPU's expert cache and the RAM tier together cannot hold every expert, and at least 16 GiB of RAM stays free after the tier and an 8 GiB margin. Then experts they miss come from RAM instead of the SSD: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on four Pro B60s took an 8K prompt from 64 to 96 tok/s, with generation about 3 % slower (manoreken2, PR #100). Where they hold every expert it stays off. A start line names the sizes and the choice. `ARC_XBUF=1` / `0` force it on / off.
- **The launchers tell the iGPUs apart by their PCI device ID**, as the engine does. Iris Xe and UHD Graphics (Tiger / Alder / Raptor Lake) were taken for Meteor Lake on Windows, with its options and its NPU setting on PCs without an NPU. On Linux they had no kind, and an Arrow Lake-S desktop was taken for the Arc 140T. "Iris Xe / UHD" is now a kind of its own.
- **The options pages** list "Prompts without H8" (`ARC_H8=0`) and "Expert file through the OS file cache" (`ARC_XBUF`).

**Please test on your machine** (paste the output into the issue):

- **A mixture-of-experts model whose experts don't fit the GPU and the RAM tier** (#4 / PR #100). The start line, then the same prompt with the new default and with `ARC_XBUF=0`:
  ```
  ./bin/runz <model.gguf> --bench-pp 8192 --n 128 2>&1 | grep -E "expert file|^pp8192|^tg128"
  ARC_XBUF=0 ./bin/runz <model.gguf> --bench-pp 8192 --n 128 2>&1 | grep -E "expert file|^pp8192|^tg128"
  ```
- **An Iris Xe / UHD or Arrow Lake-S PC:** the launcher's options page now names your GPU. Say which it shows.
